nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

Stock Audit: An Essential Business Practice

A , also known as an inventory audit, is the process of verifying a business’s physical inventory against its records. It helps identify discrepancies in stock quantity, condition, and valuation while improving inventory control and financial reporting.
Stock audits are useful for businesses involved in manufacturing, retail, wholesale, logistics, and other inventory-based activities.
Helps ensure inventory records support financial reporting.
Helps identify theft, pilferage, unauthorized movements, and discrepancies.
Helps control overstocking, understocking, and slow-moving inventory.
Supports applicable accounting, audit, lender, and regulatory requirements.
Identifies damaged, expired, obsolete, or slow-moving stock.
Conducted at scheduled intervals, such as quarterly or annually, to review inventory levels and records.
Involves regular monitoring and verification of inventory, often supported by inventory management systems.
Involves physically counting inventory and reconciling the results with stock records.
Classifies inventory based on value and movement to help prioritize verification of high-value or critical items.
Conducted without prior notice to identify discrepancies and strengthen inventory controls.
Define the audit scope and locations.
Review inventory records and supporting documents.
Assign responsibilities to the audit team.
Count or scan inventory using appropriate methods.
Check for damaged, expired, or obsolete stock.
Compare physical quantities with recorded balances.
Identify differences between physical and recorded stock.
Investigate causes such as errors, damage, theft, or misplaced inventory.
Document findings and prepare the audit report.
Suggest improvements to inventory controls and record-keeping.
Counting or recording mistakes can create discrepancies.
Unauthorized stock movements can affect inventory accuracy.
Poor monitoring can result in accumulation of unsellable stock.
Inaccurate or incomplete data makes reconciliation difficult.
